item.title: Declaration of Independence: Rare Prints on Display — Tue Sep 8, 10:00 AM — Main Library - Auditorium - Upper Corridor 2nd Floor
item.description:
We invite you to view rare 19th-century prints of the Declaration of Independence at Durham County Main Library.
As part of We the People: A Duke & Durham Initiative, Durham County Main Library and the Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University are presenting three historic copies of the Declaration of Independence on loan from the David M. Rubenstein Americana Collection. This exhibition offers a rare opportunity to explore how the nation's founding document was visually rendered and circulated in early American history.
The exhibition will feature three rare prints on loan from the David M. Rubenstein Americana Collection: a rare official full-sized 1823 facsimile engraved by William J. Stone (known as a Stone Declaration) alongside two historic broadside copies from the same era: an 1818 reproduction by calligrapher Benjamin Owen Tyler and a more ornate 1819 illustrated version published by John Binns.

item.title: Service Opportunities in Leadership (SOL) Information Session — Wed Sep 9, 5:30 PM — Sanford 223
item.description:
The Hart Leadership Program challenges students to practice the art of leadership in public life. Applications are now open for several experiential learning programs that aim to shape Duke undergraduates for reflective, ethical leadership. Our core programs involve training both inside and outside the classroom through experiential education, pedagogical preparation, reflective practice, a strong community of peers, and an aspiration to public purpose.
Service Opportunities in Leadership (SOL) is a Fellowship opportunity open to 1st, 2nd, or 3rd undergraduate students of any major who seek to deepen their capacity to build community, address complex social issues, and implement systemic change. SOL Fellows take a spring semester gateway course (PubPol 263: Leading In and With Community), receive funding for an intensive 8-week summer experience with a community partner, and complete a capstone seminar (PubPol 415: Communities of Practice).

item.title: Duke Arts at American Tobacco: Patty Griffin — Wed Sep 9, 6:30 PM — American Tobacco Campus - Lawn
item.description:
Two-time GRAMMY® Award-winning songwriter Patty Griffin is one of the most beloved voices in American folk and Americana. For more than two decades, she has written songs that capture the small moments and big emotions that shape everyday life.
The New York Times praised Griffin for writing "cameo-carved songs that create complete emotional portraits," a quality that has made her work widely recorded and deeply influential. Her 2019 self‑titled album earned the GRAMMY® for Best Folk Album, and the Americana Music Association later honored her with a Lifetime Achievement Award for Songwriting.
Griffin's songs stay with listeners long after the music ends.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Pressing Prompts Workshop (In Person) — Thu Sep 10, 10:00 AM — Rubenstein Library Carpenter Conference Room 249
item.description:
Incubated at Duke, Pressing Prompts (pressingprompts.org) is an open education resource for instructors across all disciplines who are seeking ways to integrate AI ethics into their classrooms. Unlike a static set of "best practices," Pressing Prompts is grounded in principles of critical pedagogy and educational experimentation, encouraging instructors and students to examine how AI raises crucial questions about our academic responsibilities, knowledge, labor, judgment, and learning.
In this workshop, we will offer: a brief overview of Pressing Prompts within the larger context of AI, ethics, and education; scaffolded opportunities to experiment with Pressing Prompts to consider how it might fit into one of your classroom conversations, assignments, or larger course units; and a facilitated conversation for sharing ideas between faculty peers.
Source: Duke University

item.title: THE LONG EXHALE | A GROUP EXHIBITION — Thu Sep 10, 5:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description:
5 Points Gallery is pleased to present The Long Exhale, bringing together work by the ten artists of 5 Points Gallery. As the pace of summer begins to soften, The Long Exhale invites visitors to pause, look closely, and linger. The exhibition offers a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist offering a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, August 21, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artists. The exhibition runs from August 20 through September 12, 2026. Visit 5 Points Gallery in person or online at https://5pointsgallery.com. All work from the exhibition is available for shipping or pickup. Gallery hours: Thursdays and Fridays 5–9pm and Saturdays 1–9pm. Artists are available to talk about their work. For a private viewing, contact us at info@5pointsgallery.com.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star (Theatre for the Very Young) — Sat Sep 12, 10:00 AM — Raleigh Little Theatre
item.description:
Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star is an interactive children’s theatre piece for very young audiences, performed by two Star Keepers named Glimmer and Sparkle. It’s time for the night sky to fill with stars, but one important star — Little Star, the wishing star — is missing because Sparkle rushed through putting the stars away the previous morning and muddled everything up. What follows is a search-and-rescue adventure as the two star keepers (and the audience) hunt for Little Star, discovering along the way that all the other stars have been put in the wrong places too and need to be moved to their proper place. Audience members help the Star Keepers find and re-organize the sky just in time for nightfall so that everyone can make a wish on their favorite star. Twinkle, Twinkle explores the ideas that mistakes happen, feelings are valid, and no one has to face hard things alone – all wrapped up in a genuinely joyful romp about stars.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Sat Dec 5 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Sat Dec 5, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.description:
‘TWAS THE NIGHT BEFORE… is Cirque du Soleil’s first holiday show, based on the classic poem “A Visit from Saint Nicholas” by Clement Clarke Moore. Memorable lines from this cherished classic inspired Cirque’s story about a jaded young girl who rediscovers the magic of the holidays.
A festive flurry of love and cheer created especially for families, ‘TWAS THE NIGHT BEFORE… features thrilling acrobatics, lovable characters - and a soundtrack including holiday classics re-invented by Cirque du Soleil. The show was conceived and is directed by Cirque du Soleil Senior Artistic Director James Hadley, a 25-year veteran of circus productions and live theater.
This show will be in town for 17 performances across nine days. Note that showtimes vary. Get your tickets here!

item.title: Dorrance Dance The Nutcracker Suite — Sat Dec 5, 7:00 PM — Memorial Hall
item.description:
Holiday traditions have a way of bringing people together. The best ones feel familiar and fresh at the same time.
Dorrance Dance‘s The Nutcracker Suite is set to Duke Ellington and Billy Strayhorn’s extraordinary 1960 reinterpretation of the Tchaikovsky score. Part seasonal concert, part tap ballet, the production transforms the Sugar Plum Fairy into a slinky Sugar Rum Cherry, turns the “March of the Toy Soldiers” into a swinging brass “Peanut Brittle Brigade,” and gives the original ballet’s pageant of national dances a fresh 21st-century twist.
Drawing on the rich traditions of tap dance to tell the story of one of the most beloved works in the holiday canon, The Nutcracker Suite is filled with rhythm, virtuosity, humor, and heart. The result is a performance that celebrates the joy of tradition while reminding us that the stories we return to year after year still evolve.
Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinape
